mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 jobs signals labor market strength, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under strong employment are not statistically higher than during weak employment (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% over two months indicates weakening supply-side demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than during stable INDPRO growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 250, accompanied by a rise in real activity (HOUST), creates a disinflationary environment that reduces growth expectations and yields negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 250 and HOUST > 1200 in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative when both CPIAUCSL < 250 and HOUST > 1200 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three consecutive months suggests a labor market that supports accommodative monetary policy, which is associated with positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during low-unemployment periods are not higher than during normal-range UNRATE (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in retail sales workers (PAYEMS) by over 20,000 in a month indicates consumer spending strength, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >20,000 in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during strong PAYEMS growth are not statistically higher than during moderate growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 signals a sustained supply-side weakness, which compresses earnings growth forecasts and produces negative S&P 20-day forward returns regardless of monetary policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during INDPRO weakness are not consistently negative across multiple such episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below their 2023 Q4 averages creates a dual supply shock, lowering growth expectations and resulting in negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: none (always-on signal based on rolling averages)
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during dual shock periods are not significantly lower than baseline (p > 0.05).
